We propose here the Multiple TimeLine Summarization (MTLS) task that enhances and further generalizes TLS. MTLS automatically generates a set of timelines that summarize disparate yet important stories, rather than always generating a single timeline as is in the case of TLS.
outputs: A set of timelines, each including a sequence of time/date and summary pairs
multiple timelines consisting of date-summary pairs

A set of timelines, T = {T 1 , T 2 , . . . , T k } is generated based on D, so that each timeline T i includes a sequence of time/date and summary pairs (t T i 1 , s T i 1 ), . . . , (t T i l , s T i l ) where s T i j (i = 1, . . . , k) are the summary sentences for the time t T i j (j = 1, . . . , l) and l is the length of T i .

Concatenation-based ROUGE (concat). It considers only the textual overlap... Date-agreement ROUGE (agreement). It measures both textual and temporal information overlap... Alignment-based ROUGE... Date selection (d-select). It evaluates how well the model works in selecting correct dates in the ground-truth.
We propose a quantitative evaluation measure for MTLS based on the adaptation of the previous TLS evaluation framework.
